text.headline: Timeline of Cambodia
text.text: Major events in the history of Cambodia.

events.headline: Foundation of Funan
events.text: Funan, one of the earliest known kingdoms in Southeast Asia, is established in the Mekong Delta. It plays a crucial role in trade and cultural exchange between India and China.

events.headline: Establishment of the Khmer Empire
events.text: Jayavarman II declares himself king and establishes the Khmer Empire, marking the beginning of a powerful dynasty that would dominate Southeast Asia for centuries.

events.headline: Construction of Angkor Wat
events.text: King Suryavarman II commissions the construction of Angkor Wat, which becomes a symbol of Cambodia and a masterpiece of Khmer architecture.

events.headline: Reign of Jayavarman VII
events.text: Jayavarman VII ascends to the throne and expands the empire significantly, promoting Buddhism and constructing many temples, including the Bayon.

events.headline: Fall of Angkor
events.text: The Khmer Empire begins to decline as the Thai kingdom of Ayutthaya invades Angkor, leading to the eventual abandonment of the city.

events.headline: French Protectorate Established
events.text: Cambodia becomes a protectorate of France, which leads to significant political and economic changes, as well as modernization efforts.

events.headline: Independence from France
events.text: Cambodia gains independence from French colonial rule, marking a new era in its history and the beginning of a struggle for national identity.

events.headline: Sihanouk's Reign
events.text: Norodom Sihanouk becomes the head of state, promoting a policy of neutrality during the Cold War while attempting to modernize the country.

events.headline: Khmer Republic Established
events.text: General Lon Nol overthrows Prince Sihanouk in a coup, establishing the Khmer Republic, which leads to civil unrest and the rise of the Khmer Rouge.

events.headline: Khmer Rouge Takes Power
events.text: The Khmer Rouge, led by Pol Pot, captures Phnom Penh and begins a radical transformation of Cambodian society, leading to widespread atrocities.

events.headline: Establishment of Democratic Kampuchea
events.text: The Khmer Rouge declares Democratic Kampuchea, implementing extreme communist policies that result in the deaths of an estimated 1.7 million people.

events.headline: Vietnamese Invasion
events.text: Vietnam invades Cambodia, overthrowing the Khmer Rouge regime and leading to the establishment of a new government backed by Vietnam.

events.headline: Paris Peace Agreements
events.text: The Paris Peace Agreements are signed, leading to the end of the civil war and the establishment of a framework for democratic governance in Cambodia.

events.headline: First Democratic Elections
events.text: Cambodia holds its first democratic elections under the supervision of the United Nations, leading to the establishment of a constitutional monarchy.

events.headline: Political Coup
events.text: A coup led by Hun Sen results in the consolidation of power and the establishment of a de facto one-party state, despite the presence of opposition.

events.headline: Restoration of the Monarchy
events.text: King Norodom Sihanouk is restored to the throne after years of political turmoil, symbolizing a return to stability in Cambodia.

events.headline: King Sihanouk Abdicates
events.text: King Norodom Sihanouk abdicates the throne in favor of his son, Norodom Sihamoni, marking a new chapter in the Cambodian monarchy.

events.headline: Controversial Elections
events.text: Cambodia holds elections that are marred by allegations of fraud and voter intimidation, leading to widespread protests and political unrest.

events.headline: COVID-19 Pandemic
events.text: Cambodia faces the challenges of the COVID-19 pandemic, implementing measures to control the spread of the virus while navigating economic impacts.

events.headline: 2023 General Elections
events.text: Cambodia holds general elections amid criticism of the political environment and the absence of significant opposition parties, raising concerns about democracy.
